## Steps

<figure class="story-hero"><a href="/forge-studio/media/stories/S4/01-open-studio-on-the-flows-pillar.png"><img src="/forge-studio/media/stories/S4/01-open-studio-on-the-flows-pillar.png" alt="1. Open Studio on the Flows pillar"></a></figure>

1. **Open Studio on the Flows pillar.** Three flows, all shipped with forge: one drafts a roadmap, one takes a decomposed initiative to a reviewed PR, one writes a project’s docs.
2. **Press "+ New flow".** The builder opens on a skeleton rather than an empty page: plan, then dev, then review.
3. **Name the flow and say what it is for.** A flow’s goal is not decoration: it is what every agent in it is told it is working towards, so it is written before the stations are.
4. **Drag the "architect" agent out of the palette onto the canvas, and wire it into "plan".** This is the act the builder exists for.
5. **Open Advanced and bind gitpulse’s knowledge base to the flow.** A flow that plans work on a project should read what forge already knows about it.
6. **Seed the flow’s starter agents — the roster forge offers, only if the operator asks.** The roster forge offers is not the roster you get.
7. **Press "Save Flow".** Saving is where forge judges the flow rather than the operator: the stations have to resolve to real agents, the edges have to carry artifacts the next station can read, and a name already taken is refused rather than overwritten.
8. **Check the flow came out clean and can be started.** A saved flow is not necessarily a runnable one.
9. **Open the launcher.** How a flow is launched follows from what its first station is.
10. **Point the flow at story-s4, describe the first piece of work, cap what the run may spend, and press "Start architect".** A flow built ten minutes ago is now dispatching a real Agent against a real repository, so the operator sets the ceiling before starting rather than discovering the bill afterwards.
11. **While it works, check Monitor.** Monitor is the one surface that answers "what is running, and what is stuck".
12. **Open the session from Monitor, answer the Architect's questions about the work, and wait for it to finish drafting.** The session is the same shared surface every kind of agent run uses, so a flow the operator built themselves is watched exactly the way the shipped ones are.
13. **Open the plan and stand at the verdict.** This is where S4 ends: a flow the operator assembled, linted and launched has produced a plan, and forge is holding it at a gate for a decision.
